# Online Workshop: Containers

* **December 8, 2026**
* **4 - 5:30 pm ET (1 - 2:30 pm PT)**
* **Online (Zoom) [Registration Link Coming Soon]**

## Overview

This workshop will get you started with the [_Using containers for collaborative, reproducible research_](https://www.opencasestudies.org/ocs-bio-containers/) case study, from the Open Case Studies Project. This case study uses metadata from a curated data resource for paired microbiome and metabolome datasets to explore containerization for collaborative, reproducible science, and using Docker to support scientific analyses. Rather than a step-by-step walkthrough of the case study, this workshop will orient you to the case study's motivation, questions, core goals, and initial setup tasks. We hope this will leave you with the benefits of independent learning and problem solving, while empowering you to get started.

## Intended audience

This workshop is intended for biomedical researchers who wish to expand their data science skillset to using containers to support scientific analyses and plan to work through the [_Using containers for collaborative, reproducible research_](https://www.opencasestudies.org/ocs-bio-containers/) case study.

## In preparation for this workshop

Please ensure you have done the following:

* Installed Docker Desktop
  * [For Windows](https://docs.docker.com/desktop/setup/install/windows-install/)
  * [For Mac](https://docs.docker.com/desktop/setup/install/mac-install/)
  * [For Linux](https://docs.docker.com/desktop/setup/install/linux/)

## What this workshop covers

* The problem containerization solves: Collaborative, reproducible science can be hampered by issues installing software. We'll discuss how containerization addresses this challenge, and when it's not necessarily worth the hassle. 
* Core vocabulary: We'll discuss the case study's terminology, especially terms related to containers so you can focus on the big picture.
* Getting set up: You'll make sure that Docker Desktop is installed and you can use Docker successfully.
* Using containers: You'll practice a few containerization steps related to getting started and maintenance best practices. 

## What this workshop _does not_ cover

* Data wrangling, visualization, and building Docker images. You'll complete the majority of the case study content independently using the case study materials. This workshop deliberately focuses on orientation and setup rather than providing a full walkthrough of the case study. Don't worry though because you'll have access to office hours, a community Zulip discussion forum, and the OCS community after the workshop.

## By the end of this workshop, you will:

* Understand what problem containerization solves and why it matters for reproducibility. 
* Have a working Docker Desktop.
* Have practiced steps in the containerization process.
* Know where to pick up independently in the case study.
